simple.meaning: כְּפַת (kᵉphath) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to fetter.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 3:20. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כְּפַת (H3729) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: כְּפַת (kᵉphath) / H3729 is traced through Daniel 3:20, Daniel 3:21, Daniel 3:23, Daniel 3:24 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He commanded certain mighty men who were in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and to cast them into the burning fiery furnace.

timeline.evidenceText: He commanded certain mighty men who were in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and to cast them into the burning fiery furnace.
Then these men were bound in their pants, their tunics, and their mantles, and their other clothes, and were cast into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.
These three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell down bound into the middle of the burning fiery furnace.
Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonished, and rose up in haste. He spoke and said to his counselors, “Didn’t we cast three men bound into the middle of the fire?”

definitions.full: H3729. kephath כְּפַת verb bind ( ᵑ7 id. ; Late Hebrew כָּפַת ; Syriac form knots , twist into a knot , Arabic draw together , Assyrian [ kapâtu ] II. bring together ); — Pe`il Perfect 3masculine plural פִ֫תוּ כְּ , (W CG 224 ) Dan 3:21 they were bound. Pa`el bind: Infinitive לְכַמָּתָךְ Dan 3:20 ( ל accusative of person); Passive participle plural מְכַמְּתִין bound 3:23 ; 3:24 .
